author: Tess Ikonomou
description:
Tilt comes after Michelle Landry announced she will not recontest her Queensland seat of Capricornia

  • Get our daily political email, free app or daily news podcast

The Nationals leader, Matt Canavan, will run in a lower house Queensland seat at the next federal election, in a move that may see him face off with Pauline Hanson’s chief of staff.

The announcement follows the retirement of the Capricornia MP Michelle Landry, and could result in a contest against James Ashby in a major battle for regional seats.

Continue reading...
title: Nationals leader Matt Canavan to run for lower house seat in possible showdown with One Nation’s James Ashby

author: Associated Press
description:
It is unclear if anyone on the ground was hurt and no details yet on whether anyone onboard survived

A business jet carrying nine people crashed in a Florida neighborhood on Sunday, erupting in a massive fireball.

The Learjet 60 crashed in a residential area in Florida’s Palm Beach county, federal officials said.

Continue reading...
title: Business jet carrying nine people crashes in Florida neighborhood

author: Imogen Tilden
description:
Judges hail Sofia Demetriades’s performance of Tchaikovsky’s Violin Concerto as full of insights, poetry and maturity

A teenage violinist has won the BBC Young Musician competition 2026, in the first all-female final in the competition’s 48-year history.

The judges, Joanna MacGregor, Ben Gernon and Errollyn Wallen, hailed Sofia Demetriades’s performance of Tchaikovsky’s Violin Concerto as full of insights, poetry and maturity.

Continue reading...
title: Teenage violinist wins BBC Young Musician 2026, after first all-female final

author: Roque Planas
description:
Democratic senator was at his son’s hockey game when he felt a numbness in his arm and was in Johns Hopkins

Democratic US Senator Chris Murphy has been hospitalized after suffering a stroke.

Murphy, 53, started feeling numbness in his arm while attending a his son’s hockey game on Saturday, according to the Connecticut senator’s chief of staff, Allison Herwitt. A hospital visit confirmed that Murphy had experienced a stroke.

Continue reading...
title: Connecticut senator Chris Murphy hospitalized after stroke

author: Eric Berger
description:
Voting is particularly high in states with tight Senate races that could determine which party controls the chamber

US citizens are casting ballots in record numbers ahead of the midterm elections on Tuesday, another potential indication, analysts say, of voter dissatisfaction with Republicans and Donald Trump.

Voting was particularly high in states that feature tight Senate races that could determine which party controls the chamber.

Continue reading...
title: Three key takeaways from early voting in midterm elections

author: Patrick Wintour Diplomatic editor
description:
Indirect talks run into third day with Qatar trying to negotiate release of $6bn in Iranian assets that could lead to reopening of strait

Officials from the Gulf states are “braced for the worst” as they wait for Washington’s response to an Iranian proposal that could reopen the strait of Hormuz before the US midterm elections on Tuesday.

Indirect talks in Doha ran into a third day on Sunday, with Qatar trying to negotiate the release of more than $6bn in Iranian assets, which could lead to the reopening of the strait of Hormuz and the restart of negotiations on Iran’s nuclear programme.

Continue reading...
title: Negotiators ‘braced for worst’ over US-Iran talks to reopen strait of Hormuz

author: Chris Hippensteel
description:
Stevens lost the party’s Michigan primary by a close margin and had refused to endorse El-Sayed, with tensions between the two high

Congresswoman Haley Stevens, who lost the Michigan Democratic Senate primary to Abdul El-Sayed, endorsed his Republican rival, Mike Rogers, in an extraordinary rebuke of her party’s nominee on the eve of the midterm elections.

Her endorsement came in a video posted to X after she attended an event with Rogers at the predominantly Black Perfecting church in Detroit on Sunday. The event marks a stunning political moment in Michigan, where control of the seat could be crucial to Democratic party.

Continue reading...
title: Democrat Haley Stevens endorses Abdul El-Sayed’s Republican rival Mike Rogers

author: Jessica Elgot Deputy political editor
description:
On Brexit, devolution and investment, the former chancellor is eerily in tune with the man who sacked her

  • Reeves says UK’s future is in the EU

Which senior politician has argued that “Brexit did deep damage” and that the government seeks “not to turn back the clock but to look toward a new and stable, future relationship?”

It was not Andy Burnham, who has been the torchbearer for thinking the unthinkable on Brexit since he became prime minister. Instead, these are the words of the former chancellor Rachel Reeves, in a lecture six months ago.

Continue reading...
title: How Rachel Reeves has mapped out economic agenda for Andy Burnham’s government

author: Daniel A Medina with photographs by Eric Ruby
description:
Residents of Menomonie mounted a successful protest against a huge campus in the city as national resistance to the AI boom grows

In the spring of 2025, Sydney Brennan was riding high. The 22-year-old was finishing college and was a newly elected councilwoman in Menomonie, a city of about 17,000 in the lush plains of north-western Wisconsin.

Weeks into the new job, she was invited to a meeting with consultants pitching a $1.6bn AI hyperscale datacenter campus that an undisclosed big tech company wanted to build just outside of town. The project’s numbers were eye-opening: a 320-acre site that would use an estimated 75,000 gallons of water per day, making it the most significant development in Menomonie’s nearly 150-year history.

Continue reading...
title: How a small Wisconsin city scuttled a secretive $1.6bn datacenter project

author: Haroon Siddique Legal affairs correspondent
description:
Arrests come ahead of Wednesday’s supreme court challenge to the ban on the direct action group

Police have said they arrested 325 people on Saturday at a demonstration outside the US embassy in London against the proscription of Palestine Action.

In updated arrest figures released on Sunday, the Metropolitan police said 320 people were detained outside the building in Battersea, south London, for allegedly expressing support for an organisation banned under the Terrorism Act.

Continue reading...
title: Police detain 325 people at pro-Palestine Action protest at US embassy in London

author: Lauren Almeida
description:
New electricity generating capacity would enable north-east to attract investment for major datacentre projects

National Grid has taken a step towards building Britain’s biggest electricity substation on Teesside, which could supply power to a vast neighbouring datacentre as the UK races to expand its AI infrastructure.

Last week the company agreed to purchase 29.5 hectares (73 acres) of land at Dorman Point on a site owned by Teesworks, a local private-public partnership. The deal was first reported by Sky News.

Continue reading...
title: National Grid to site biggest substation on Teesside, near planned AI datacentre

author: Guardian staff and agencies
description:
Mann taken to hospital with superficial injury after weapon accidentally discharged while holstered

Hollywood director Michael Mann has been taken to the hospital following an apparently accidental shooting at a Los Angeles gun range, according to the Associated Press.

Mann, 83, reportedly shot himself in the leg while at the The Range LA. The news was first reported on celebrity website TMZ. He sustained what his representative described as a superficial injury after a weapon accidentally discharged while holstered.

Continue reading...
title: Director Michael Mann accidentally shoots himself in the leg at gun range

description:
Police say three separate shootings occurred in Deep Ellum neighborhood and are trying to determine if they’re related

Police in Dallas say four people are dead and 15 are injured following separate shootings in a Dallas neighborhood. It was among several violent incidents nationwide on Halloween weekend.

The police chief, Daniel Comeaux, said police are still trying to determine if the shootings in the Deep Ellum neighborhood were related.

Continue reading...
title: Multiple shootings in Dallas leave four dead and 15 injured on Halloween night

author: Charlie Moloney
description:
Police searching for ‘unknown group’ that gained entry to property in Chandler’s Ford on Saturday night

Five teenage boys were stabbed at a Halloween party, after an “unknown group” gained entry to the event on a residential road, police have been told.

The boys, all aged 16 and 17, were found injured after police were called to a report five teenagers had been stabbed at a property in Chandler’s Ford near Eastleigh, Hampshire, just after 10.30pm on Saturday.

Continue reading...
title: Five teenagers hurt in stabbing at Halloween party in Hampshire

author: Chris Hippensteel
description:
Senator was allegedly targeted in ballot-stacking ploy by his Democratic opponent to peel away votes from him

Senator Dan Sullivan, the Alaska Republican allegedly targeted in a ballot-stacking ploy by his Democratic opponent, Mary Peltola, told CNN this morning that he would accept the results of his upcoming election.

According to a recent New York Times investigation, aides from Peltola’s campaign recruited another man who shared Sullivan’s name to join the race in a ploy to peel away votes from the Republican incumbent.

Continue reading...
title: Republican senator Dan Sullivan says he will accept Alaska election results

author: Haroon Siddique
description:
Dr Marta Shahbazi was travelling to a conference to receive award for scientific excellence in developmental biology

An “inspiring” University of Cambridge scientist died in the Spanish train collision on Wednesday that killed at least 69 people.

Dr Marta Shahbazi, an affiliate associate professor at the Cambridge Stem Cell Institute and a group leader at the city’s Medical Research Council Laboratory of Molecular Biology (LMB), was travelling on one of the trains involved in the crash near Urda in Toledo province.

Continue reading...
title: Tributes paid to ‘inspiring’ Cambridge scientist who died in Spain train crash

author: Jessica Elgot Deputy political editor
description:
Adrian Ramsay says some new members would be ‘more at home’ in Your Party or Socialist Workers party

The former Green party leader Adrian Ramsay has said the party must fix its internal democracy to avoid a takeover by the hard left, saying that some new members “might be more at home” in Your Party or the Socialist Workers party.

Ramsay, who has been critical of the handling of the row over a “Zionism is racism” motion passed at the Green party conference, said there were a “small number” of individuals who used “divisive” tactics to influence the party’s agenda.

Continue reading...
title: Green party must avoid being taken over by hard left, says former leader

author: Agencies
description:
• Eight injured in shooting outside Legion Field

  • Annual game draws huge crowds to Birmingham

One person was killed and eight others were wounded in a mass shooting outside Legion Field after the annual Magic City Classic football game on Saturday night, police in Birmingham, Alabama, said.

Michael Pickett, chief of the Birmingham Police Department, said most spectators and families had left the stadium property after the game, but the shooting happened nearby, where vendors were set up along Graymont Avenue.

Continue reading...
title: One person killed in shooting outside Magic City Classic football game in Alabama

author: Gaya Gupta
description:
In state that become ‘ground zero’ for discrimination against south Asians, experts say they are seeing voters motivated to fight back

Last winter, while Pooja Sethi was canvassing to become the Democratic candidate for the Texas house of representatives, she received a text from a staff member alerting her to a post on X. The Turning Point USA influencer Savanah Hernandez – a Trump supporter known for creating videos that target immigrants – had posted a photo of Sethi’s campaign banner with the caption: “Welcome to politics in Texas.”

The post went viral.

Continue reading...
title: ‘There’s a lot of hate’: rightwing racism stirs south Asian mobilization in Texas

author: Jonathan Barrett Business editor
description:
Centre of downturn shifts away from Sydney and Melbourne, but after such strong growth most homeowners still sit on sizeable gains

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Australian home values have dropped for a seventh consecutive month, with prices in the capital cities now falling at the fastest pace in 40 years as rising mortgage rates scare off buyers.

Cotality data shows the centre of the downturn is also shifting away from Sydney and Melbourne toward the mid-sized state capital cities, with Brisbane and Perth leading October’s declines.

Continue reading...
title: Home values fall for seventh consecutive month as interest rates dent demand

author: Henry Belot and Penry Buckley
description:
Exclusive: Mark Jones, once on track for one of the Liberal party’s most powerful roles, is now instrumental in One Nation’s expansion

  • Get our daily political email, free app or daily news podcast

In 2023, a young and ambitious Liberal moderate was on the brink of securing one of the most powerful roles in the party: state director of the New South Wales branch. Three years later, he is playing a key role in selecting and vetting One Nation candidates determined to beat his former colleagues.

Multiple Liberal sources familiar with recruitment for the position, which involves running election campaigns and managing fundraising, confirm Mark Jones was among the final three candidates for the role before his career advancement was
title: Former NSW Liberal leads overhaul of One Nation candidate selection process

author: Tory Shepherd
description:
Chair of National Gallery’s First Nations advisory group says the technology is undermining artists’ agency and the authenticity of their work

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

AI is taking First Nations art and turning it into “Temu slop”, the Pitjantjatjara artist Sally Scales has said.

Scales, the chair of the National Gallery of Australia’s First Nations advisory group, said the technology is undermining the agency of First Nations artists and the authenticity of their work and represents a “a theft” of cultural knowledge.

Continue reading...
title: AI is stealing Indigenous Australian art and churning out ‘Temu slop’, artist says

author: Lisa Cox
description:
Exclusive: Move to scrap legal requirement to set aside water for environment is ‘extreme even for the NT CLP government’, green group says

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

The Northern Territory government has been accused of making a “blatant and shameless” attack on nature by planning to delete a legal requirement that water must be allocated to the environment.

In what has been described as the latest in a series of attacks on the environment by the NT’s Country Liberal party, the Finocchiaro government plans to change water rules that govern how much ground and surface water industry can take.
title: Northern Territory water plan condemned as ‘blatant and shameless’ attack on nature

author: Bethan McKernan Wales correspondent
description:
UPCCs in Holyhead, Tremadog and Bangor may shut as Betsi Cadwaladr University health board struggles with funding and recruitment

A struggling Welsh health board may close urgent primary care centres at three hospitals, citing funding and recruitment issues, prompting widespread criticism.

Betsi Cadwaladr University health board, which serves about a quarter of Wales’s population, said it was consulting on ending urgent primary care centres (UPCCs) at Ysbyty Penrhos Stanley in Holyhead, Ysbyty Alltwen in Tremadog and Ysbyty Gwynedd in Bangor by April 2027.

Continue reading...
title: Welsh health board may close urgent primary care centres at three hospitals

author: Rich Tenorio
description:
The conflict that tore through New England 350 years ago was the bloodiest per capita in colonial or US history

Massachusetts is proud of its ties to the American Revolution. From Paul Revere’s Ride to the siege of Boston, the past year-plus has been devoted to celebrating 250 years of US independence. Yet during this time, the state, and New England in general, has given far less attention to an older, more complex remembrance: The 350th anniversary of King Philip’s war.

King Philip, or Metacom, was an Indigenous leader from the Pokanoket people. Alarmed by English colonists’ infringement of Indigenous rights, from seizing land to proselytizing, Metacom led an alliance of New England tribes – including the Pokanoket, Nipmuc and Narragansett – in an existential struggle for control of the region. He gave his name to the conflict, but paid with his life – as did many others, soldiers and civilians alike. With an estimated 800 dead on the colonial side, and three to five
title: Spirit of 1676: remembering the Native American cataclysm of King Philip’s war

author: Jessica Elgot Deputy political editor
description:
Chancellor John Healey fails to guarantee equalisation with adult wage will happen in timeframe set out in manifesto

Labour looks less likely to meet its manifesto pledge to equalise the minimum wage for younger workers before the next election, after the chancellor failed to guarantee the rise would happen within that timeframe.

John Healey said on Sunday the government was still committed to the increase but failed to spell out when it would be achieved. In the budget, a rise in the minimum wage was handed to adults – to £13.21– and under-20s – to £11.27 – but a larger rise for younger workers would have been needed to move towards equalisation.

Continue reading...
title: Labour’s pledge to level-up minimum wage for under-20s before next election in doubt

author: Jessica Elgot Deputy political editor
description:
Tory leader says apology would be ‘navel-gazing distraction’ and would be used as lever for financial compensation

Kemi Badenoch has said an apology for Britain’s role in the transatlantic slave trade would be a “navel-gazing distraction”, describing slavery as an evil “in which people from every continent and region participated”.

Speaking to broadcasters on Sunday, Badenoch also questioned whether it was worth future leaders attending the Commonwealth summit, given that it was now dominated by calls for reparations.

Continue reading...
title: Britain should not issue apology over slave trade, says Kemi Badenoch

author: Gwyn Topham Transport correspondent
description:
Mayor questions impact on air quality, congestion and jobs as government poised to allow driverless vehicles in capital

London’s mayor has called for a cap on the numbers of robotaxis on its streets, with the UK government poised to allow fully driverless vehicles to operate in the capital.

Sadiq Khan said politicians had failed to “grasp the pace of change” from the technology, which could threaten jobs and increase congestion in the city, and questioned whether the rules for autonomous cars were fit for purpose.

Continue reading...
title: Sadiq Khan calls for cap on numbers of robotaxis on London streets

author: Diane Taylor
description:
Guardian understands Home Office continues to detain dozens of people, with one group forcibly removed this week

The Home Office is still putting asylum seekers on to planes to France weeks after the controversial scheme to remove them ended, the Guardian has learned.

The “one in, one out” scheme was announced by the French president, Emmanuel Macron, and the former prime minister Keir Starmer in July 2025. It aimed to deter small boats crossing the Channel to the UK from northern France, with some asylum seekers arriving here forcibly returned to France while a similar number in northern France were brought legally to the UK.

Continue reading...
title: Asylum seekers still being sent to France under ‘one in one out’ weeks after scheme ended

author: Guardian staff and agencies
description:
Former chancellor says leaving European Union has made Britain ‘poorer, weaker and less secure’

The former chancellor Rachel Reeves has argued the UK’s future should be inside the EU, saying Brexit has made the UK “poorer, weaker and less secure”.

Writing in the Sunday Times, the Labour former cabinet minister said she welcomed “Andy Burnham’s leadership” after remarks made by the prime minister in recent days fuelled questions about the
title: Rachel Reeves says UK’s future is in EU as she backs Andy Burnham on Brexit

author: Rob Davies
description:
Hundreds of adult gaming centres in England have bingo licences that still qualify them for discounted business rates

Hundreds of high street “slot farms” could continue claiming a discount on their business rates, unless the government closes a loophole that allows them to pose as bingo halls.

John Healey singled out adult gaming centres (AGCs) in his first budget this week, in which he increased duty on slot machine takings from 20% to 25%, claiming he was “raising taxes on gambling to support good growth on every high street”.

Continue reading...
title: High street ‘slot farms’ could evade budget tax rise through bingo hall loophole

author: Guardian staff and agencies
description:
Cryptocurrency exchange says withdrawals expected to resume on Sunday as FBI blames North Korean state-sponsored group TraderTraitor

Cryptocurrency exchange Binance says it has replaced 90% of the ⁠amount stolen after a record $6.3bn hack of its platform by a group the FBI identified as being backed by North Korea.

The remaining 10% of tokens are less liquid, meaning they ⁠may take ​longer to buy, the company said in a post on X on Saturday. Co-CEO Richard Teng said separately that the company was “committed to covering the ⁠remaining 10%” and that “users will not bear the financial impact of this incident”.

Continue reading...
title: Binance says 90% of losses from $6.3bn hack covered as FBI says North Korea behind attack
